comments.concern: Switching IsShiftState() from GetKeyState to GetAsyncKeyState changes the semantics of Shift detection and risks reintroducing stuck-Shift / mis-read navigation regressions.
comments.detail: GetAsyncKeyState reports the real-time physical key state at call time, not the state synchronized to the message being processed like GetKeyState. IsShiftState now feeds both _initialShiftState (captured in ShowToolbar) and the ProcessNextChar hardware fallback; a physical/logical timing mismatch can make a capital-accent summon read as backward navigation, or leave Shift 'stuck' — exactly the class of bugs in #45936/#47034. Justify why async is preferred here for both call sites.

comments.concern: Reordering ProcessNextChar makes StartSelectionFromTheLeft take precedence over the Left/Right trigger keys, silently changing arrow-key initial selection behavior.
comments.detail: Previously StartSelectionFromTheLeft only affected the Space trigger; Left/Right always started at (len/2)-1 and len/2. The new if/else-if chain checks StartSelectionFromTheLeft before Left/Right, so with that setting enabled arrow keys now start at index 0. This is a behavior change for existing users that isn't called out — confirm it's intended and covered by tests.

comments.concern: New Space+Shift branch (shiftPressed ? last : 0) introduces Shift handling that is inconsistent with the Left/Right branches, which ignore shiftPressed for the initial index.
comments.detail: Shift is overloaded (capitals + reverse navigation). Only the Space branch honors shiftPressed for the initial index; Left/Right do not. Combined with the new hardware-shift fallback (shiftPressed || isHardwareShiftPressed), a capital-accent summon via Space could jump to the last element unexpectedly. Verify against the _initialShiftState guard so a capital summon isn't misread.

comments.concern: GetDisplayCoordinates now returns physical/raw coordinates (removed the '/ dpi'), but WPF's this.Left/Top are no longer used — position is applied via SetWindowPos while WPF still tracks a stale DIP position.
comments.detail: SetWindowPosition passes the physical point straight to SetWindowPos, yet the WPF window's Left/Top properties are never updated. WPF layout (SizeToContent, DPI changes, SizeChanged) still reasons in DIPs from the old Left/Top, so the OS position and WPF's logical position disagree, risking a jump/flicker on the wrong monitor — the multi-monitor/DPI failure class (#40498/#44980). Keep WPF's logical position in sync or document why SetWindowPos alone is safe.

comments.concern: GetDisplayMaxWidth now divides physical width by DPI, but the coordinate space of characters.MaxWidth vs the SetWindowPos-based positioning should be verified for consistency.
comments.detail: The fix correctly converts raw px to DIP for WPF MaxWidth (which expects DIPs) and subtracts the DIP ScreenMinPadding — this addresses the too-wide popup (#44332). However positioning uses raw px multiplied by dpi in Calculation while MaxWidth is DIP; ensure the window's measured DIP width fed into GetDisplayCoordinates stays within this DIP max so clamping still prevents off-screen rendering on mixed-DPI monitors.

comments.concern: GetDpiForWindow → GetDpiForMonitor(MDT_EFFECTIVE_DPI) is the right direction, but confirm the monitor handle and per-monitor-DPI-awareness assumptions.
comments.detail: Positioning must use the active window's monitor DPI. GetDpiForMonitor uses the handle from MonitorFromWindow(active) — good — but it requires the process to be per-monitor DPI aware and Win8.1+. The 96 fallback on non-S_OK is reasonable; verify behavior on secondary/mixed-DPI monitors since this feeds both size and position calculations.

comments.concern: Replacing VirtualizingStackPanel with a plain StackPanel realizes every item, which can regress performance/memory for letters with many variants.
comments.detail: The distilled slow-popup/lag regressions (#39852/#42821) were tied to work on the keystroke hot path. Realizing all containers (needed for ScrollIntoView/ActualWidth measurement) is acceptable for small sets but should be confirmed not to lag for the largest mappings; note this is on the render path each summon.

comments.concern: Adding ScrollViewer.HorizontalScrollBarVisibility=Auto on a ListBox with IsHitTestVisible=False produces a non-interactive scrollbar and may consume layout space.
comments.detail: Because the ListBox is IsHitTestVisible=False, the scrollbar is purely decorative (selection is keyboard-driven), which may confuse users and its track can affect measured height/width. Confirm the scrollbar doesn't clip the 48px item row or throw off the characterName MaxWidth binding to characters.ActualWidth.

comments.concern: The description row keeps a hardcoded MinWidth=600 while the character row is now clamped to the screen-derived max width — MinWidth=600 can still exceed a small/low-DPI screen and render off-screen.
comments.detail: GetDisplayMaxWidth now correctly caps the characters area, but the Grid.Row=1 name panel forces MinWidth=600 independent of screen width. On narrow displays this can make the overall window wider than the monitor, partially defeating the off-screen fix and the clamp guardrail.

comments.concern: Window_SizeChanged unconditionally re-invokes SetWindowPosition on every size change while SizeToContent=WidthAndHeight, risking repositioning churn/flicker or feedback loops.
comments.detail: With SizeToContent the window resizes as items/description change; each resize repositions via SetWindowPos, which combined with OnDpiChanged and the initial off-screen move can cause multiple repositions per summon. Confirm this doesn't cause visible jitter or recursive layout, especially across monitor boundaries.

comments.concern: The off-screen pre-position uses SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN minus 1000 (physical px) via SetWindowPos, but the hwnd==0 fallback sets this.Left/Top which are DIPs — mixed coordinate spaces.
comments.detail: When the HWND isn't yet created, the code assigns physical-derived offsets to WPF Left/Top (DIPs). This is a rare path but is coordinate-space-inconsistent and could place the window somewhere unexpected. Also verify the virtual-screen metrics are in the same space SetWindowPos expects under per-monitor DPI awareness.

comments.concern: PowerAccent_OnChangeDisplay indexes _powerAccent.CharacterDescriptions[_selectedIndex] guarded only against chars.Length, not CharacterDescriptions.Length.
comments.detail: The active branch checks _selectedIndex < chars.Length before reading CharacterDescriptions[_selectedIndex]. If the characters and descriptions arrays can ever diverge in length (e.g., description build deferred/lazy per #48937), this can throw. Bound-check against CharacterDescriptions.Length as the OnSelectionCharacter handler now correctly does.

comments.concern: OnDpiChanged recomputes size/position, but SetWindowPosition reads Application.Current.MainWindow.Content.ActualWidth which may not yet reflect the new DPI layout at the moment the event fires.
comments.detail: If ActualWidth/Height are stale during the DPI transition, GetDisplayCoordinates (which multiplies window size by the new dpi) can compute an off position. Ensure layout is updated before reading ActualWidth, or reposition after the subsequent layout pass.

comments.concern: New Microsoft.Windows.CsWin32 PackageReference is added without a Version and with PrivateAssets — confirm it resolves via central package management and doesn't pull WinRT/build props into the UI project.
comments.detail: Omitting Version assumes Directory.Packages.props defines it; if not, the build breaks. Also, per module convention interop/WinRT concerns are kept out of certain projects — verify CsWin32 source-gen here is intended and that x64+ARM64 Debug/Release all build, consistent with the native-tooling-bump evidence expectation.

comments.concern: _initialShiftState is captured via IsShiftState() (now GetAsyncKeyState) in ShowToolbar, adding a second, hardware source of Shift state alongside the keyboard hook's tracked shift.
comments.detail: There are now two Shift sources (the hook-provided shiftPressed and the async hardware read). This overlaps with the native listener's m_leftShiftPressed/m_rightShiftPressed logic that only observes Shift after the toolbar is visible. Confirm the managed fallback doesn't double-count or conflict with the hook's shift model and doesn't re-open the SHIFT-lock regression.

comments.concern: SetWindowsSize now also sets this.MaxWidth on the window; combined with SizeToContent and the characters MaxWidth this could over-constrain and clip the description row.
comments.detail: Setting both characters.MaxWidth and window MaxWidth to the same DIP value, while Row=1 has MinWidth=600 and a MaxWidth bound to characters.ActualWidth, creates competing constraints. Verify the description text (with TextTrimming + Wrap + MaxHeight=36) renders correctly and the window isn't clipped when descriptions are long.
